easy.def: The sound you make when you talk or sing.
examples: I have a loud voice.
Use your inside voice.
Her voice is sweet.

more.def: The sound that comes from a person's mouth when they speak or sing.
examples: The teacher has a calm, friendly voice.
I heard a voice calling from the garden.
Her singing voice is clear and high.

easy.def: A mountain that can shoot out hot melted rock.
examples: The volcano had smoke on top.
Hot lava came out of the volcano.
The island has a volcano.

more.def: A mountain with an opening where melted rock, ash, and gas can burst out.
examples: When the volcano erupted, lava flowed down its sides.
The island was formed by a volcano long ago.
Ash from the volcano covered the nearby town.
Turn down the volume.
The volume is loud.
The radio's volume is low.

more.def: How loud or quiet a sound is.
examples: Turn down the volume of the TV.
The volume on the radio was too high.
The teacher asked us to lower our volume.
The volume of the tank is large.
The cup's volume is one cup.
Find the volume.

more.def: The amount of space that something takes up or holds.
examples: The volume of the tank is fifty gallons.
We measured the volume of water in the cup.
The box has a large volume.
I read the first volume.
The set has ten volumes.
The library has old volumes.

more.def: One book in a set, or a book.
examples: I read the first volume of the series.
The scientist kept a volume of notes.
The library has old volumes of the news.

easy.def: A person who does a job for free because they want to.
examples: A volunteer read to us.
She is a volunteer at the library.
Volunteers cleaned the park.

more.def: A person who chooses to do a job without pay to help others.
examples: A volunteer read stories to the kids at the library.
Volunteers helped clean up the beach.
The hospital has many volunteers.
I volunteered to help.
She volunteers at the shelter.
He volunteered to carry the bags.

more.def: To offer to do something without being asked or paid.
examples: He volunteered to carry the heavy bags.
She volunteers at the animal shelter on Saturdays.
I volunteered to clean the board.

easy.def: To throw up food from your stomach.
examples: I felt sick and vomited.
The dog vomited.
He vomited.

more.def: To bring up food from your stomach through your mouth.
examples: The baby vomited after drinking too fast.
I felt sick and almost vomited.
The dog vomited on the rug.

easy.def: To choose by raising a hand or marking a paper.
examples: We vote for class pet.
She voted for the red team.
Raise your hand to vote.

more.def: To show your choice by raising a hand or marking a ballot.
examples: Our class voted for a new pet.
Adults vote to choose a mayor.
Everyone voted to go to the park.

easy.def: A choice you make in a group.
examples: My vote is for pizza.
Each person gets a vote.
The vote was close.

more.def: A choice that you show in a group decision.
examples: My vote is for the pizza party.
Each student gets one vote.
The vote was close, but the red team won.
He made a vow.
The vow was kept.
She made a vow to help.

more.def: A very serious promise that you make.
examples: He made a vow to keep the secret.
The knights made a vow to protect the king.
She kept her vow to visit her grandmother each week.
I vow to help.
She vowed to be kind.
He vowed to try again.
She vowed to keep the secret.
He vowed to try harder next time.
The knight vowed to protect the village.

easy.def: A long trip on a ship or in space.
examples: The ship went on a long voyage.
We read about a voyage to the moon.
The voyage took many days.

more.def: A long journey, especially by sea or through space.
examples: The voyage across the ocean took three weeks.
The explorers set off on a voyage around the world.
The spacecraft began its long voyage to Mars.
